summary: Cold review of the canonical web conversion build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/60-twentieth-after-pentecost.md for DOCUMENT_ROOT src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/60-twentieth-after-pentecost. Its conversion hash, as research/web-artifact.json records it and as the file on disk gives it, is SHA-256 071cf8ce54ed16ad029e2817d7ab00b89bd92133de94c2ae73b0302bce4f0717, which matches REVIEW_INPUTS. It is the only web output for the leaf: no synthesis or homily leaf exists under build/web. tools/check-web-edition reports the leaf eligible. Running tools/web-edition again from the current sources (pandoc 3.11, pinned Markdown 3.10.3 venv, output to scratch) reproduced it byte for byte, with every converter audit exiting 0. The reviewed research PDF (build/claude/.../60-twentieth-after-pentecost.pdf, SHA-256 f1a99182...87c4, 31 pages) and all 32 hashes in research/artifacts.json match the files on disk, so the conversion and the PDF share the same render inputs. Text: a word-sequence diff of the Markdown against the PDF text layer leaves only layout differences. These are running heads and folios, the printed contents list replaced by [TOC], table cells extracted in another order, the comparison table's repeated continuation head, the text layer's V for the versicle glyph, and the H1 and italic subject line that the converter takes from the PDF's own title metadata, as in the installed Nineteenth Sunday edition. A punctuation-sensitive check found 253 of 258 prose paragraphs verbatim in the PDF. The other five are the two metadata lines and three paragraphs whose only difference is where the text layer puts the versicle glyph. All 193 \latin and 119 \work arguments are italic in the rendered page. Structure: rendered with the site's own extensions, there are 10 h2 and 47 h3 headings, the same hierarchy as the PDF's .toc plus the References subheads. Each of the three readings is its own h2 (lane-* anchors), and each closes with its four senses as a Literal/Allegorical/Moral/Anagogical definition list (3 dl, 12 dt/dd). The ten proper-<key> anchors match the manifest's element keys and sit on single-element headings. There are no duplicate ids, and the 10 TOC links resolve. The 27 quotation environments render as 27 blockquotes, with 14 small-caps witness heads and the ℣ glyph displaying. The ten-row map and the seven-row comparison table are complete. The Scriptural Date and Location dossier follows the maintainer's 2026-09-23 pattern: seven per-passage tables carrying the generated chronology payloads, with each prose note, and the Introit's and Gospel's italic narrated-event rows, set beneath its table. There is no TeX debris, unresolved reference, trailing whitespace, model, run, machine or provenance metadata. The revision timestamp 2026-10-07T20:03:52Z (the PDF's ModDate) and the rights colophon are present. The three external URLs resolve. Browser review: the page was rendered through tools/public-alpha render_page and the site layout and stylesheet, then viewed in headless Chromium. At 1280 px there is no overflow. At a 390 px iframe viewport there is no page-level horizontal scroll, and the dossier sets each row as two lines of two. Limit: at phone width the map and comparison tables scroll horizontally inside their frames. That is the stylesheet's general table handling, measured the same on the installed Nineteenth Sunday edition, and is not a defect of this conversion. The page was not installed into web/ or published, and no tracked file was changed. Verdict: PASS, no findings.
